title: Betfred to shut 132 shops after gambling tax hikes

evidence_packet.title: Betfred to shut 132 shops after gambling tax hikes
evidence_packet.lead: The bookmakers says it had 'no choice' after rises in gambling tax, national insurance and wages
evidence_packet.summary: The bookmakers says it had 'no choice' after rises in gambling tax, national insurance and wages
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Betfred plans to shut 132 shops and cut more than 600 jobs from September, as the gambling firm blamed higher taxes and economic uncertainty The company said it has launched a consultation over the closures, which will hit more than a tenth of its betting shops The move will leave Betfred with around 1,100 shops across the UK The closure plans come on the back of tax increases announced by the previous chancellor, which Fred Done described as the "biggest threat" to the industry in his 57 years Measures announced in last year's autumn budget saw an increase in remote gaming duty from 21% to 40%, while there will also be a new online sports betting duty of 25%, which will cover all sports except horse racing, from 2027 Betfred also highlighted pressure from other tax increases including the rise in National Insurance contributions and changes to thresholds

title: Fraudster Pamela Gwinnett arrested at Manchester Airport

evidence_packet.title: Fraudster Pamela Gwinnett arrested at Manchester Airport
evidence_packet.lead: Pamela Gwinnett is extradited back to the UK after she conned a vulnerable pensioner out of £300k
evidence_packet.summary: Pamela Gwinnett is extradited back to the UK after she conned a vulnerable pensioner out of £300k
evidence_packet.evidence_text: To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played A woman who abused her position as a carer to con almost £300,000 out of a vulnerable pensioner then fled to Tenerife has been arrested on her return to the UK Pamela Gwinnett was convicted of theft and fraud after she plundered the life savings of 89-year-old Joan Green from Chorley, Lancashire after becoming her carer She flew to Tenerife in April 2025 while on bail and was sentenced in her absence to six years in jail Gwinnett was extradited back to the country after an investigation by UK and Spanish authorities and was escorted into a police van on arrival at Manchester Airport on Thursday Gwinnett will now have to serve her six-year sentence, and is set to appear at Manchester Magistrates Court later in relation to her failing to appear at court previously

title: Manchester stabbing: Man, 19, in 'life-threatening' condition

evidence_packet.title: Manchester stabbing: Man, 19, in 'life-threatening' condition
evidence_packet.lead: He was found on Church Street in the Northern Quarter after police were called at about 12:50 BST
evidence_packet.summary: He was found on Church Street in the Northern Quarter after police were called at about 12:50 BST
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A teenager has been taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries after being stabbed in Manchester city centre, police have said The 19-year-old was found on Church Street in the Northern Quarter after Greater Manchester Police (GMP) were called at about 12:50 BST Officers had received reports of an "ongoing incident" in the area, said a GMP spokesperson No arrests have been made over the stabbing and investigations are ongoing Emergency services vehicles including a helicopter could be seen in the busy Northern Quarter earlier as police responded to the incident A police cordon is in place along Church Street, a busy thoroughfare in the area

title: Greenfield villagers say moorland fires getting worse every year

evidence_packet.title: Greenfield villagers say moorland fires getting worse every year
evidence_packet.lead: Those living in the shadow of the still-raging Dove Stone fire say they feel "hurt" by the lasting damage
evidence_packet.summary: Those living in the shadow of the still-raging Dove Stone fire say they feel "hurt" by the lasting damage
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Villagers living in the shadow of a Greater Manchester moorland fire that continues to burn after three weeks say they "feel like they've been hurt" after the treasured landscape went up in flames Firefighters are still tackling the blaze at Dove Stone Reservoir in Saddleworth, which broke out on 11 July after a period of hot weather and low rainfall, before merging with other wildfires For those living in nearby Greenfield, road closures and the near-constant movement of fire engines have become a regular sight Deborah Hill, who works in interior design shop My Secret Boutique, said: "I think it's worrying about what is up there with the animals and wildlife and how long it will take for it to recover." She told the Local Democracy Reporting Service : "The fires are happening every year and they are getting worse every year. This is a bad one because it has gone on for weeks. That is worrying." While things have quietened now, she said: "Every day you generally see about six fire engines going past. You might see at least two police cars. Sirens all the time. It's like being in the city

title: TikToker faces police probe over secret filming using Meta 'smart glasses'

evidence_packet.title: TikToker faces police probe over secret filming using Meta 'smart glasses'
evidence_packet.lead: The "content maker" published videos of encounters with young women and a female Sikh shop worker where he talked of a plot to "breed out the white race"
evidence_packet.summary: The "content maker" published videos of encounters with young women and a female Sikh shop worker where he talked of a plot to "breed out the white race"
evidence_packet.evidence_text: TikToker faces police probe over secret filming using Meta 'smart glasses' - BBC News Image source, YouTube Image caption, Margerison filmed a series of encounters around Scotland using Oakley Meta glasses which contain tiny cameras Published 30 July 2026 Updated 6 hours ago A TikToker who used Meta "smart glasses" to secretly film members of the public, shop workers and ferry staff during a road trip around Scotland is being investigated by police. Footage posted by Scott Margerison includes him swearing at a stranger, making sexualised comments about young women and an interaction with a Sikh shopkeeper where he talks about a plan to "breed out the white race". In another video Margerison, from Rochdale, recorded a tour of the bridge of the CalMac ferry Loch Seaforth, prompting the firm to suspend the popular visits. Police Scotland confirmed it had received complaints and was reviewing footage to establish if any criminality was involved. BBC Scotland News has attempted to contact Margerison for comment. Margerison, who also posts on Instagram and YouTube, has built up the vast majority of his social media audience on TikTok using the alias E Dobbin. In his videos he frequently approaches strangers and starts bizarre conversations. Image source, YouTube Image caption, Margerison, seen here in Dunoon, with a microphone clipped onto his beard In late June and early July he toured Scotland in a white Ford Transit van, visiting various locations including Dunoon, Glencoe, John O'Groats, Skye, Uist, Barra and Lewis. While many of his videos feature harmless banter, others have a darker side, particularly when he encounters young women or people from ethnic minorities. In one video, the 42-year-old makes sexualised comments about the appearance of two teenagers who he spot

title: Oldham woman becomes world's first to receive new cancer therapy

evidence_packet.title: Oldham woman becomes world's first to receive new cancer therapy
evidence_packet.lead: Tracy Tomlinson was offered the clinical trial for ovarian cancer at The Christie hospital in Manchester
evidence_packet.summary: Tracy Tomlinson was offered the clinical trial for ovarian cancer at The Christie hospital in Manchester
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman with advanced ovarian cancer has become the first patient in the world to receive a pioneering new therapy Tracy Tomlinson was given the drug at The Christie hospital in Manchester as part of a clinical trial evaluating a new type of treatment for several types of cancer The therapy, known as ZI-MA4-1, will be tested on people with ovarian cancer, lung cancer, sarcomas and head and neck cancer in a trial led by the Christie, and a site at the Royal Marsden in London The 58-year-old, from Chadderton, Oldham, decided almost straight away she was going to go for it, she said, although she admitted it was a "little bit scary" being the first person to have the treatment Many people in the early stage study - which is primarily focused on safety - have few other options for survival Tomlinson has already beaten the odds in staying alive, having undergone surgery and several rounds of chemotherapy since she was diagnosed in 2020

evidence_packet.summary: Work to improve Macclesfield Station was supposed to have been completed in the spring
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A train company has confirmed that work to upgrade a Cheshire railway station on the West Coast Main Line will be delayed by six months Work to improve the entrance and upgrade the ticket office at Macclesfield Station began last November and was supposed to have been completed in the spring but Avanti West Coast has now said it will now not be completed until the autumn Richard Slater, the managing director of Henbury Travel travel agents in the town, said: "People want to get a drink or buy a newspaper but there's nowhere to get refreshments, so it is very disappointing that the gateway to the town is being disrupted." title: Atherton dad relieved family is safe after fire devastates house

evidence_packet.title: Atherton dad relieved family is safe after fire devastates house
evidence_packet.lead: Derek Smith, 30, ' was thinking the worst' when a fire broke out at his Atherton home on Monday
evidence_packet.summary: Derek Smith, 30, ' was thinking the worst' when a fire broke out at his Atherton home on Monday
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Atherton dad relieved family is safe after fire devastates house - BBC News Image source, Derek Smith Image caption, Derek Smith (left) said wife, Kylie (right), and daughter, Ellie May, were at home when the fire broke out By Georgie Docker North West Published 30 July 2026 A father whose family lost all their belongings in a devastating fire at their home earlier this week said he was lucky his wife and 12-year-old daughter, as well as their cats, "made it out alive" and has vowed to make the most of life in the future. A blaze broke out in the kitchen of Derek Smith's home, on Thomas Street in Atherton, Wigan, shortly before 11:30 BST on Monday. The 30-year-old described it as "one of the most tragic days of our lives", but said it "could have been a lot worse" and has made him see life "in a whole new way". He said: "We are just lucky to be able to tell our story." Image source, Derek Smith Image caption, 'It was one of the most tragic days of our lives,' Derek said. A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said four fire engines attended the fire, which began in the kitchen of the property on 27 July. Derek, a mental health volunteer, said he left the house at 08:00 BST, leaving his wife and daughter at home for the day. Less than four hours later, Derek received a call from his wife - but she was so distressed he could not understand what she was saying. "She wasn't making any sense - she was distraught, she was crying her eyes out. "I could hear my daughter was crying her eyes out too." Aware something was wrong, Derek called his mother, who told him the house was on fire. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Villagers living in the shadow of a Greater Manchester moorland fire that continues to burn after three weeks say they "feel like they've been hurt" after the treasured landscape went up in flames Firefighters are still tackling the blaze at Dove Stone Reservoir in Saddleworth, which broke out on 11 July after a period of hot weather and low rainfall, before merging with other wildfires For those living in nearby Greenfield, road closures and the near-constant movement of fire engines have become a regular sight Deborah Hill, who works in interior design shop My Secret Boutique, said: "I think it's worrying about what is up there with the animals and wildlife and how long it will take for it to recover." She told the Local Democracy Reporting Service : "The fires are happening every year and they are getting worse every year. This is a bad one because it has gone on for weeks. That is worrying." While things have quietened now, she said: "Every day you generally see about six fire engines going past. You might see at least two police cars. Sirens all the time. It's like being in the city

evidence_packet.lead: A TikToker who used Meta "smart glasses" to secretly film members of the public, shop workers and ferry staff during a road trip around Scotland is being investigated by police Footage posted by Scott Margerison includes him swearing at a stranger, making sexualised comments abou
evidence_packet.summary: A TikToker who used Meta "smart glasses" to secretly film members of the public, shop workers and ferry staff during a road trip around Scotland is being investigated by police Footage posted by Scott Margerison includes him swearing at a stranger, making sexualised comments abou
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A TikToker who used Meta "smart glasses" to secretly film members of the public, shop workers and ferry staff during a road trip around Scotland is being investigated by police Footage posted by Scott Margerison includes him swearing at a stranger, making sexualised comments about young women and an interaction with a Sikh shopkeeper where he talks about a plan to "breed out the white race" In another video Margerison, from Rochdale, recorded a tour of the bridge of the CalMac ferry Loch Seaforth, prompting the firm to suspend the popular visits Police Scotland confirmed it had received complaints and was reviewing footage to establish if any criminality was involved BBC Scotland News has attempted to contact Margerison for comment Margerison, who also posts on Instagram and YouTube, has built up the vast majority of his social media audience on TikTok using the alias E Dobbin

title: Oldham woman becomes world's first to receive new cancer therapy

evidence_packet.title: Oldham woman becomes world's first to receive new cancer therapy
evidence_packet.lead: A woman with advanced ovarian cancer has become the first patient in the world to receive a pioneering new therapy Tracy Tomlinson was given the drug at The Christie hospital in Manchester as part of a clinical trial evaluating a new type of treatment for several types of cancer
evidence_packet.summary: A woman with advanced ovarian cancer has become the first patient in the world to receive a pioneering new therapy Tracy Tomlinson was given the drug at The Christie hospital in Manchester as part of a clinical trial evaluating a new type of treatment for several types of cancer
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman with advanced ovarian cancer has become the first patient in the world to receive a pioneering new therapy Tracy Tomlinson was given the drug at The Christie hospital in Manchester as part of a clinical trial evaluating a new type of treatment for several types of cancer The therapy, known as ZI-MA4-1, will be tested on people with ovarian cancer, lung cancer, sarcomas and head and neck cancer in a trial led by the Christie, and a site at the Royal Marsden in London The 58-year-old, from Chadderton, Oldham, decided almost straight away she was going to go for it, she said, although she admitted it was a "little bit scary" being the first person to have the treatment Many people in the early stage study - which is primarily focused on safety - have few other options for survival Tomlinson has already beaten the odds in staying alive, having undergone surgery and several rounds of chemotherapy since she was diagnosed in 2020

title: Work to upgrade station delayed by six months

evidence_packet.title: Work to upgrade station delayed by six months
evidence_packet.lead: A train company has confirmed that work to upgrade a Cheshire railway station on the West Coast Main Line will be delayed by six months Work to improve the entrance and upgrade the ticket office at Macclesfield Station began last November and was supposed to have been completed i
evidence_packet.summary: A train company has confirmed that work to upgrade a Cheshire railway station on the West Coast Main Line will be delayed by six months Work to improve the entrance and upgrade the ticket office at Macclesfield Station began last November and was supposed to have been completed i
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A train company has confirmed that work to upgrade a Cheshire railway station on the West Coast Main Line will be delayed by six months Work to improve the entrance and upgrade the ticket office at Macclesfield Station began last November and was supposed to have been completed in the spring but Avanti West Coast has now said it will now not be completed until the autumn Richard Slater, the managing director of Henbury Travel travel agents in the town, said: "People want to get a drink or buy a newspaper but there's nowhere to get refreshments, so it is very disappointing that the gateway to the town is being disrupted." Avanti West Coast said: "We're continuing to work closely with our contractors to deliver the redevelopment works at Macclesfield station and would like to thank customers for their patience and understanding." The operator added: "Parts of the project are nearing completion and we're looking forward to welcoming customers and the community into the new station environment soon, which will provide an improved gateway to the town "We know many people are keen to understand when the work will be finished and work is expected to be completed in autumn."

evidence_packet.title: Atherton dad relieved family is safe after fire devastates house
evidence_packet.lead: A father whose family lost all their belongings in a devastating fire at their home earlier this week said he was lucky his wife and 12-year-old daughter, as well as their cats, "made it out alive" and has vowed to make the most of life in the future A blaze broke out in the kitc

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A father whose family lost all their belongings in a devastating fire at their home earlier this week said he was lucky his wife and 12-year-old daughter, as well as their cats, "made it out alive" and has vowed to make the most of life in the future A blaze broke out in the kitchen of Derek Smith's home, on Thomas Street in Atherton, Wigan, shortly before 11:30 BST on Monday The 30-year-old described it as "one of the most tragic days of our lives", but said it "could have been a lot worse" and has made him see life "in a whole new way" He said: "We are just lucky to be able to tell our story." A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said four fire engines attended the fire, which began in the kitchen of the property on 27 July Derek, a mental health volunteer, said he left the house at 08:00 BST, leaving his wife and daughter at home for the day

Nancy Swanick, had run the Peveril of the Peak on Great Bridgewater Street, Manchester, since 1971. The mother-of-three died on Tuesday aged 96. The historic pub, nicknamed The Pev, has just been named the best pub in the UK by Time Out. The Grade II-listed venue has been part of Manchester since 1820 and is known for its green-tiled exterior. Her grandson Michael Swanick said "the world's a sadder place now" and she was an "amazing woman". Image source, Google Image caption, The Pev has been part of Manchester since 1820 The 47-year-old told BBC Radio Manchester: "We are still dealing with the shock of it. "It has been a hell of a week. " The solicitor added: "She was almost born to be the perfect host. "She made a great impression on everybody. "My nan was the life and soul of the pub and we want to cherish everything Nancy brought to it and the city. "All the tributes have been breathtaking. "She was a larger than life character and she was dedicated to The Pev." On the Time Our award, Swanick said: "She was really chuffed about it. "We want everyone to raise a glass to Nancy this weekend as she deserves it." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 How many people voted in the Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026? The turnout for every borough More than half a million people voted in the by-election View Image Counting taking place for the mayoral ele News Simon Coyle Content editor | Head of search 14:52, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 15:33, 31 Jul 2026 Hundreds of thousands of people have cast their vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral election In total, 538,659 took part in the by-election to elect a new mayor, with more than 2.1 million people eligible to vote. This means the overall turnout for the region was just 25.14%, lower than in the 2017, 2021, and 2024 elections The low turnout is believed to be due to apathy towards politics and a lack of engagement with the mayoral role, as well as people being away for the summer and scores of students who could have voted going home during the university break Across the region, Trafford had the highest turnout at 35%, with Oldham the lowest on 22% The by-election was called in June following former mayor Andy Burnham's election has Makerfield MP

title: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 turnout confirmed

evidence_packet.title: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 turnout confirmed
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 turnout confirmed More than two million people were eligalbe to vote in the election View Image Counting taking place at Co-op Live (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Even News Simon Coyle Content edi
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 turnout confirmed More than two million people were eligalbe to vote in the election View Image Counting taking place at Co-op Live (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Even News Simon Coyle Content edi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 turnout confirmed More than two million people were eligalbe to vote in the election View Image Counting taking place at Co-op Live (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Even News Simon Coyle Content editor | Head of search 14:05, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 14:20, 31 Jul 2026 The turnout for the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election has been confirmed Just 25.14% of those eligible turned out to vote in the election to select the region's new mayor. This amounts to 538,659 people It compares against a turnout of 32.05% at the last mayoral election in 2024, 34.7% in 2021 and 28.9% in 2017 In total 2,142,779 people were able to vote in the ballot from across the region, which includes the boroughs of Bolton , Bury , Oldham , Manchester, Rochdale , Salford , Stockport , Tameside , Trafford and Wigan Apathy towards politics and a lack of engagement with the mayoral role are believed to have played a part, as well as people being away for the summer and scores of students who could have voted going home during the university break

evidence_packet.lead: The University of Manchester Family of Sir Bernard Lovell speak out to condemn funding cuts to Jodrell Bank observatory EXCLUSIVE: 'No one, but no one thinks that this is a good idea' Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 13:14, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 13:1 The family of the late scien
evidence_packet.summary: The University of Manchester Family of Sir Bernard Lovell speak out to condemn funding cuts to Jodrell Bank observatory EXCLUSIVE: 'No one, but no one thinks that this is a good idea' Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 13:14, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 13:1 The family of the late scien
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Family of Sir Bernard Lovell speak out to condemn funding cuts to Jodrell Bank observatory EXCLUSIVE: 'No one, but no one thinks that this is a good idea' Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 13:14, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 13:1 The family of the late scientist Sir Bernard Lovell have spoken out to condemn multi-million pound Government funding cuts to Jodrell Bank - the space observatory he created "No one, but no one thinks that this is a good idea," Sir Bernard's daughter, Judy Spence, told the Manchester Evening News today on behalf of generations of the family Ms Spence went on to challenge senior members of the Science and Technology Facilities Council - which has announced a vast cost-cutting drive - to visit Jodrell Bank and meet scientists and staff 'involved in the extraordinary work there'. "They will be inspired," she added The M.E.N. has launched a campaign to save deep space science at the observatory - and the working life of its iconic telescope, The Lovell Telescope A pioneering figure of British science, Sir Bernard was a founder of Jodrell Bank. Working with engineer Charles Husband, they conceived and designed what was then the world's biggest steerable radio telescope

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tameside Urgent appeal for girl, 16, who vanished two weeks ago with no phone or money Family and friends haven't heard from Jessica since her disappearance and are 'incredibly concerned' about her View 2 Images Jessica, 16, is missing from Tameside ( News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 12:59, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 12:59, 31 Jul 2026 Police have shared a fresh appeal for help to trace a 16-year-old girl who went missing from Tameside more than two weeks ago with no phone and no money Jessica vanished on Thursday, July 16. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires MP calls to suspend sale of disposable BBQs amid huge wildfires across UK Several major wildfires have occurred across the UK this summer News Emily Parker Shopping Writer 12:56, 31 Jul 2026 View 2 Images A huge wildfire began at Tintwistle Moor A Derbyshire MP is calling on major UK retailers and supermarkets to suspend the sale of disposable barbecues this summer in a bid to reduce the risk of wildfires across the country It follows the break out of two large-scale wildfires across Derbyshire and Greater Manchester in recent weeks, at Tintwistle Moor, near Glossop and Dovestone Reservoir, near Greenfield, in Oldham Firefighters are continuing to work on controlling the huge wildfire which broke out at Dovestone Reservoir three weeks ago , with experts warning that it will likely take years for the land to recover from the blaze. A major incident was also declared at Tintwistle Moor, where t This week a major incident was also declared in Suffolk after a wildfire broke out at Dunwich Heath, near Leiston, which spread to cover an area as big as 210 football pitches in just 24 hours With disposable barbecues being a leading cause of wildfires in the UK, High Peak MP Jon Pearce is now calling on retailers to withdraw disposable barbecues from shop shelves over the remaining summer months

Rudakubana has been charged with: assault on an emergency worker on May 6, 2025, attempted grievous bodily harm on May 8, 2025, unauthorised possession of an offensive weapon in prison on He was given a life sentence with a minimum term of 52 years for the murders of Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, Bebe King, six, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, and the attempted murder of eight other children and two adults in Southport This week marked two years since he carried out the attack at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class on July 29, 2024. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Flanked by police and surrounded by cameras, the moment fraudster Pamela Gwinnett was arrested Pamela Gwinnett, 63, fled to Tenerife in a bid to escape justice - but returned to Manchester Airport last night News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking Pamela Gwinnett, dubbed the 'Black Widow', fled the UK for Tenerife while awaiting trial for theft and fraud by abuse of position in 2025. In her absence, the 63-year-old was handed a six-year jail sentence A huge operation was launched by Greater Manchester Police and the National Crime Agency to bring Gwinnett back to the UK to face justice. Earlier this month she was detained by Spanish Police and last night (July 30), she landed at Manchester Airport where she was arrested GMP has today (July 31) released body-worn camera footage the moment she was arrested and put into the back of a police van outside Terminal 3. Gwinnett was flanked by two armed National Crime Agency officers as she was escorted out of the building Police then met her outside, with the footage showing the moment she was arrested. Gwinnett, who was wearing sunglasses, a leopard print jacket, capri pants and gold trainers, replied 'OK' as an officer outlined the details of her arrest The footage also showed several photographers surrounding her. Officers then carried out a search on Gwinnett before putting her into the back of a police van

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires Incredible drone footage shows huge scale of Tintwistle Moor wildfire The fire service said 'steady progress' is being made on the moorland as the A628 Woodhead Pass reopens News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 08:48, 31 Jul 2026 I A wildfire at Tintwistle Moor, near Glossop, first started burning on June 24. A major incident was then declared in the area on July 12 as hotspots took hold of a huge area of the moorland Emergency crews have been on the scene for weeks tackling the fire in challenging conditions amid dry and warm weather. Yesterday (July 30) the Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service (DFRS) shared drone footage, taken by the Derby Mountain Rescue Team, which showed the scale of the m The service said previously that the fire, which sent huge plumes of smoke across Greater Manchester at its height, was estimated to have burned 606 hectares - equivalent to 900 football pitches. The footage showed hotspots burning in the peat on the moorland The fire service said in the update on Wednesday that 'steady progress continues to be made' as crews work across four main sectors. DFRS said: "The incident remains divided into four sectors at present, allowing resources to be deployed effectively and ensuring all affected area "While overall progress remains positive, on-ground teams have seen a slight increase in hotspots within the Featherbed Moss sector following a shift in wind direction. Crews are actively targeting these areas and are monitoring conditions closely

title: Greater Manchester mayoral election LIVE results and updates as turnout announced as lowest in history

evidence_packet.title: Greater Manchester mayoral election LIVE results and updates as turnout announced as lowest in history
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 LIVE Updated 3 mins ago Greater Manchester mayoral election LIVE results and updates as turnout announced as lowest in history The Greater Manchester mayoral election results will be announced later on Friday T Polling stations closed at 1
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 LIVE Updated 3 mins ago Greater Manchester mayoral election LIVE results and updates as turnout announced as lowest in history The Greater Manchester mayoral election results will be announced later on Friday T Polling stations closed at 1
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 LIVE Updated 3 mins ago Greater Manchester mayoral election LIVE results and updates as turnout announced as lowest in history The Greater Manchester mayoral election results will be announced later on Friday T Polling stations closed at 10pm on Thursday, with the count taking place from 9am on Friday. Hundreds of thousands of votes will be counted at Co-op Live, with the result not expected until at least early afternoon And it could be even later if no candidate receives more than 50 per cent of the vote - meaning the second round votes will need to be counted At 2pm on Friday, the turnout was revealed - 25.14pc - with 538,659 votes cast from an electorate of 2,142,779. That's the lowest in history for the mayoral role in the region. At the 2024 election, the turnout was 32.05pc. It was 28.9pc in 2017; and 34.7pc in 2021 Apathy towards politics and a lack of engagement with the mayoral role are believed to have played a part, as well as people being away for the summer and scores of students who could have voted going home during the university break The election was held using the supplementary vote system , which meant that people were able to vote for two candidates, a first and second preference

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Dovestones Map shows scale of destruction following huge Dovestone Reservoir wildfire Use our interactive map to see the extent of the damage caused by the wildfire at the popular beauty spot in Saddleworth View 3 Images Firefighters continue to work News Miranda Pell Search and Discover Writer 06:28, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 07:01, 31 Jul 2026 Firefighters continue to work on controlling a huge wildfire, near Greenfield, Oldham , which has been burning for nearly three weeks One woman has been remanded in custody after being charged with arson in connection with the moorland fire at the Greater Manchester beauty spot. Shania Care-Slede, 20, appeared at Manchester Magistrates' Court on July 14 after being charged with two offences She has been charged with one count of arson, while being reckless as to whether life was endangered, and one count of dangerous driving. Experts have warned that the fires have caused "mass fatality and a state of ecological emergency" . evidence_packet.title: Oldham woman the first person in the world to receive groundbreaking cancer therapy at The Christie
evidence_packet.lead: Oldham Oldham woman the first person in the world to receive groundbreaking cancer therapy at The Christie 'I often think, 'I'm still here', and that's helped me think.
evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Oldham woman the first person in the world to receive groundbreaking cancer therapy at The Christie 'I often think, 'I'm still here', and that's helped me think. 'why can't I still be here in 10 years?' News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 06:22, A woman from Greater Manchest
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Oldham woman the first person in the world to receive groundbreaking cancer therapy at The Christie 'I often think, 'I'm still here', and that's helped me think. 'why can't I still be here in 10 years?' News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 06:22, A woman from Greater Manchester with advanced ovarian cancer has become the first patient in the world to receive a pioneering new therapy. Tracy Tomlinson, 58, was given the drug at the Christie in Manchester as part of a clinical trial evaluating a new type of treatment for sev The therapy, known as ZI-MA4-1, will be tested on people with ovarian cancer, lung cancer, sarcomas and head and neck cancer in a trial led by the Christie, with a site also at the Royal Marsden in London. Many people in the study have few other options for survival Mrs Tomlinson, from Chadderton, Oldham, has already beaten the odds of staying alive, having undergone surgery and several rounds of chemotherapy since she was diagnosed in 2020 The new therapy works by combining two powerful methods in fighting cancer. Firstly, it harnesses the body’s natural killer (NK) cells, which are specialist immune cells that destroy abnormal ones Secondly, T-cell receptors (TCRs) on the cells are engineered to recognise and target tumours producing a protein called Mage-A4. Mage-A4 is found in several types of cancer and experts believe it is an ideal target for attacking abnormal cells

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 How many people voted in the Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026? The turnout for every borough More than half a million people voted in the by-election View Image Counting taking place for the mayoral ele News Simon Coyle Content editor | Head of search 14:52, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 15:33, 31 Jul 2026 Hundreds of thousands of people have cast their vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral election In total, 538,659 took part in the by-election to elect a new mayor, with more than 2.1 million people eligible to vote. This means the overall turnout for the region was just 25.14%, lower than in the 2017, 2021, and 2024 elections The low turnout is believed to be due to apathy towards politics and a lack of engagement with the mayoral role, as well as people being away for the summer and scores of students who could have voted going home during the university break Across the region, Trafford had the highest turnout at 35%, with Oldham the lowest on 22% The by-election was called in June following former mayor Andy Burnham's election has Makerfield MP

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 turnout confirmed More than two million people were eligalbe to vote in the election View Image Counting taking place at Co-op Live (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Even News Simon Coyle Content editor | Head of search 14:05, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 14:20, 31 Jul 2026 The turnout for the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election has been confirmed Just 25.14% of those eligible turned out to vote in the election to select the region's new mayor. This amounts to 538,659 people It compares against a turnout of 32.05% at the last mayoral election in 2024, 34.7% in 2021 and 28.9% in 2017 In total 2,142,779 people were able to vote in the ballot from across the region, which includes the boroughs of Bolton , Bury , Oldham , Manchester, Rochdale , Salford , Stockport , Tameside , Trafford and Wigan Apathy towards politics and a lack of engagement with the mayoral role are believed to have played a part, as well as people being away for the summer and scores of students who could have voted going home during the university break

evidence_packet.lead: The University of Manchester Family of Sir Bernard Lovell speak out to condemn funding cuts to Jodrell Bank observatory EXCLUSIVE: 'No one, but no one thinks that this is a good idea' Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 13:14, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 13:1 The family of the late scien
evidence_packet.summary: The University of Manchester Family of Sir Bernard Lovell speak out to condemn funding cuts to Jodrell Bank observatory EXCLUSIVE: 'No one, but no one thinks that this is a good idea' Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 13:14, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 13:1 The family of the late scien
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Family of Sir Bernard Lovell speak out to condemn funding cuts to Jodrell Bank observatory EXCLUSIVE: 'No one, but no one thinks that this is a good idea' Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 13:14, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 13:1 The family of the late scientist Sir Bernard Lovell have spoken out to condemn multi-million pound Government funding cuts to Jodrell Bank - the space observatory he created "No one, but no one thinks that this is a good idea," Sir Bernard's daughter, Judy Spence, told the Manchester Evening News today on behalf of generations of the family Ms Spence went on to challenge senior members of the Science and Technology Facilities Council - which has announced a vast cost-cutting drive - to visit Jodrell Bank and meet scientists and staff 'involved in the extraordinary work there'. "They will be inspired," she added The M.E.N. has launched a campaign to save deep space science at the observatory - and the working life of its iconic telescope, The Lovell Telescope A pioneering figure of British science, Sir Bernard was a founder of Jodrell Bank. Working with engineer Charles Husband, they conceived and designed what was then the world's biggest steerable radio telescope

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fuel Prices The cheapest place to get petrol and diesel in Greater Manchester today - Friday, 31 July Use our interactive widget to fill your car for less Comments News Paul Gallagher and Ryan Price 12:55, 31 Jul 2026 View Image Fuel prices displayed The cheapest place to fill up your car with petrol in Greater Manchester today (Friday, 31 July) is at a Costco Wholesale garage in Oldham According to the latest data supplied by retailers, a driver in an average family car could save up to £22 by filling up at this forecourt - compared to the most expensive petrol station The Costco Wholesale garage at The Broadway in Chadderton is charging motorists 147.9p per litre, which means it would cost £91 to fill up an average 55 litre tank. This is based on a feed of live petrol prices which is published by the government Here are the cheapest places to top your car with petrol today The most expensive filling station in Greater Manchester is the BP station at the Birch Service Area in Heywood . The cost of standard petrol at this station is 185.9p, meaning it would cost a total of £113 to fill up an average family car at this forecourt

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires MP calls to suspend sale of disposable BBQs amid huge wildfires across UK Several major wildfires have occurred across the UK this summer News Emily Parker Shopping Writer 12:56, 31 Jul 2026 View 2 Images A huge wildfire began at Tintwistle Moor A Derbyshire MP is calling on major UK retailers and supermarkets to suspend the sale of disposable barbecues this summer in a bid to reduce the risk of wildfires across the country It follows the break out of two large-scale wildfires across Derbyshire and Greater Manchester in recent weeks, at Tintwistle Moor, near Glossop and Dovestone Reservoir, near Greenfield, in Oldham Firefighters are continuing to work on controlling the huge wildfire which broke out at Dovestone Reservoir three weeks ago , with experts warning that it will likely take years for the land to recover from the blaze. A major incident was also declared at Tintwistle Moor, where t This week a major incident was also declared in Suffolk after a wildfire broke out at Dunwich Heath, near Leiston, which spread to cover an area as big as 210 football pitches in just 24 hours With disposable barbecues being a leading cause of wildfires in the UK, High Peak MP Jon Pearce is now calling on retailers to withdraw disposable barbecues from shop shelves over the remaining summer months

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Southport Southport killer Axel Rudakubana charged with three assaults on staff at HMP Belmarsh Rudakubana has also been charged with unauthorised possession of an offensive weapon in prison News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 11:14, 31 Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has been charged with three assaults on staff at HMP Belmarsh Rudakubana has also been charged with unauthorised possession of an offensive weapon in prison. The 19-year-old was charged on Tuesday over the three separate alleged attacks in 2025, the Metropolitan Police said He is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court via videolink on Friday, September 11. Rudakubana has been charged with: assault on an emergency worker on May 6, 2025, attempted grievous bodily harm on May 8, 2025, unauthorised possession of an offensive weapon in prison on He was given a life sentence with a minimum term of 52 years for the murders of Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, Bebe King, six, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, and the attempted murder of eight other children and two adults in Southport This week marked two years since he carried out the attack at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class on July 29, 2024. In May last year, it was alleged he used a kettle in his cell to heat water up and then poured boiling water over a prison officer

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Flanked by police and surrounded by cameras, the moment fraudster Pamela Gwinnett was arrested Pamela Gwinnett, 63, fled to Tenerife in a bid to escape justice - but returned to Manchester Airport last night News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking Pamela Gwinnett, dubbed the 'Black Widow', fled the UK for Tenerife while awaiting trial for theft and fraud by abuse of position in 2025. In her absence, the 63-year-old was handed a six-year jail sentence A huge operation was launched by Greater Manchester Police and the National Crime Agency to bring Gwinnett back to the UK to face justice. Earlier this month she was detained by Spanish Police and last night (July 30), she landed at Manchester Airport where she was arrested GMP has today (July 31) released body-worn camera footage the moment she was arrested and put into the back of a police van outside Terminal 3. Gwinnett was flanked by two armed National Crime Agency officers as she was escorted out of the building Police then met her outside, with the footage showing the moment she was arrested. Gwinnett, who was wearing sunglasses, a leopard print jacket, capri pants and gold trainers, replied 'OK' as an officer outlined the details of her arrest The footage also showed several photographers surrounding her. Officers then carried out a search on Gwinnett before putting her into the back of a police van

evidence_packet.title: Rochdale shisha lounge closed after deadly gas put customers' lives in danger
evidence_packet.lead: Rochdale Rochdale shisha lounge closed after deadly gas put customers' lives in danger The venue was found to have exposed both customers and workers to excessive levels of carbon monoxide Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 10:28, 31 Jul 202 A Greater Manchester Shisha
evidence_packet.summary: Rochdale Rochdale shisha lounge closed after deadly gas put customers' lives in danger The venue was found to have exposed both customers and workers to excessive levels of carbon monoxide Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 10:28, 31 Jul 202 A Greater Manchester Shisha
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Rochdale shisha lounge closed after deadly gas put customers' lives in danger The venue was found to have exposed both customers and workers to excessive levels of carbon monoxide Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 10:28, 31 Jul 202 A Greater Manchester Shisha lounge has been closed after excessive levels of carbon monoxide were found. Phantom The Lounge on Maclure Road, Rochdale , were ordered to close by Rochdale Council's environmental health service The closure order was granted at Manchester Magistrates' court on July 24 following evidence submitted by environmental health officers, alongside support from Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service officers and Greater Manchester Police The order for the premises to close came following a routine inspection, which found that Phantom the Lounge had been illegally operating due to smoking taking place on site in a substantially closed area, Rochdale Council said The council's environmental officers identified this as a clear violation of the Smoke-Free regulations under the Health Act 2006 In addition to the illegal smoking, hazardous practices in the kitchen were found to have put customers and workers at risk due to "excessively high levels of CO" (carbon monoxide) on site

Those who fly from the airport will benefit from the changes made as part of the airport’s £1.5billion transformation program Terminal 2 has been renovated and extended, with new additions including the Great Northern Market, a foodhall-style eating spot where diners can choose from a range of kitchens serving up pizza, Greek food and more. Meanwhile in the Boutique Mall area passengers can browse luxur Passengers flying from Terminal 3, which now only serves Ryanair, can visit the new sports bar, Sporting Chance, which has more than 500 seats. She was flanked by two armed National Crime Agency officers A smile as she exited quickly turned into a solemn look once she spotted cameras pointed at her. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics Mayors to get bigger share of income tax as part of Government's shake up of power Prime Minister Andy Burnham will give local leaders more flexibility to keep their revenue but it's not clear yet how much they will receive. Iram Ramzan repor News Iram Ramzan 22:30, 30 Jul 2026 Regional mayors will get a share of income tax revenue in what the Government says is the biggest transfer of power, funding and responsibility from Westminster in a generation The new system will give local leaders more freedom and flexibility to keep the revenue generated in their regions without being told by Whitehall how to spend it From April 2027, mayors will retain a greater share of business rates and from spring 2028 they will receive a share of income tax revenue. It is not yet clear what percentage of income tax the mayors will receive, but further details are expected during the autumn budget Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: “I said we'd take power out of Westminster and carry it into every postcode in the country. Today, we make good on that promise “Under our plans, more of the taxes raised in a community will stay in that community. Soon, every local leader will have the power and resources to improve public transport, build homes and create jobs

title: Greater Manchester mayoral election LIVE results and updates as turnout announced as lowest in history

evidence_packet.title: Greater Manchester mayoral election LIVE results and updates as turnout announced as lowest in history
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 LIVE Updated 4 mins ago Greater Manchester mayoral election LIVE results and updates as turnout announced as lowest in history The Greater Manchester mayoral election results will be announced later on Friday T Polling stations closed at 1
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 LIVE Updated 4 mins ago Greater Manchester mayoral election LIVE results and updates as turnout announced as lowest in history The Greater Manchester mayoral election results will be announced later on Friday T Polling stations closed at 1
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 LIVE Updated 4 mins ago Greater Manchester mayoral election LIVE results and updates as turnout announced as lowest in history The Greater Manchester mayoral election results will be announced later on Friday T Polling stations closed at 10pm on Thursday, with the count taking place from 9am on Friday. Hundreds of thousands of votes will be counted at Co-op Live, with the result not expected until at least early afternoon And it could be even later if no candidate receives more than 50 per cent of the vote - meaning the second round votes will need to be counted At 2pm on Friday, the turnout was revealed - 25.14pc - with 538,659 votes cast from an electorate of 2,142,779. That's the lowest in history for the mayoral role in the region. At the 2024 election, the turnout was 32.05pc. It was 28.9pc in 2017; and 34.7pc in 2021 Apathy towards politics and a lack of engagement with the mayoral role are believed to have played a part, as well as people being away for the summer and scores of students who could have voted going home during the university break The election was held using the supplementary vote system , which meant that people were able to vote for two candidates, a first and second preference

The turnout for every borough More than half a million people voted in the by-election View Image Counting taking place for the mayoral ele News Simon Coyle Content edi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 How many people voted in the Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026? The turnout for every borough More than half a million people voted in the by-election View Image Counting taking place for the mayoral ele News Simon Coyle Content editor | Head of search 14:52, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 15:33, 31 Jul 2026 Hundreds of thousands of people have cast their vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral election In total, 538,659 took part in the by-election to elect a new mayor, with more than 2.1 million people eligible to vote. This means the overall turnout for the region was just 25.14%, lower than in the 2017, 2021, and 2024 elections The low turnout is believed to be due to apathy towards politics and a lack of engagement with the mayoral role, as well as people being away for the summer and scores of students who could have voted going home during the university break Across the region, Trafford had the highest turnout at 35%, with Oldham the lowest on 22% The by-election was called in June following former mayor Andy Burnham's election has Makerfield MP

It came after he learned she wanted to divorce him A court heard how Ahmad was controlling, abusive and violent towards Mrs Rafay over a number of years, including 'kerb-crawling' as she walked to walk; taking control of her wages; and repeatedly assaulting her. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 turnout confirmed More than two million people were eligalbe to vote in the election View Image Counting taking place at Co-op Live (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Even News Simon Coyle Content editor | Head of search 14:05, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 14:20, 31 Jul 2026 The turnout for the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election has been confirmed Just 25.14% of those eligible turned out to vote in the election to select the region's new mayor. This amounts to 538,659 people It compares against a turnout of 32.05% at the last mayoral election in 2024, 34.7% in 2021 and 28.9% in 2017 In total 2,142,779 people were able to vote in the ballot from across the region, which includes the boroughs of Bolton , Bury , Oldham , Manchester, Rochdale , Salford , Stockport , Tameside , Trafford and Wigan Apathy towards politics and a lack of engagement with the mayoral role are believed to have played a part, as well as people being away for the summer and scores of students who could have voted going home during the university break

evidence_packet.summary: Courts The web of lies of a man who murdered his wife Syed Ahmad savagely attacked his wife Anam Rafay at their home in Wythenshawe earlier this year View 5 Images Syed Ahmad (Image: Greater Manchester Police) News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:00, 30 Jul 2026 Updated 13:38, 31 Ju
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The web of lies of a man who murdered his wife Syed Ahmad savagely attacked his wife Anam Rafay at their home in Wythenshawe earlier this year View 5 Images Syed Ahmad (Image: Greater Manchester Police) News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:00, 30 Jul 2026 Updated 13:38, 31 Jul 2026 Surrounded by police, Syed Ahmad's lies began. "Self defence, self defence," he said. "She attacked me." His wife's lifeless body lay on the floor in the rain yards away. Anam Rafay had suffered up to 40 stab wounds. The 36-year-old had tried to leave their Wythenshawe home - and her abusive and controlling spouse - after falling in love with another man Mrs Rafay repeatedly served divorce papers on Ahmad, 45. He repeatedly said he would change Then, on January 27 this year, as she stood by the sink, she was savagely attacked - wildly stabbed and left to die. Callous Ahmad told a subsequent murder trial: "I love my wife." Jurors heard that in the wake of the brutal killing he was seen smirking. The trial was later told he messaged family members: "I have killed my wife."

evidence_packet.summary: The University of Manchester Family of Sir Bernard Lovell speak out to condemn funding cuts to Jodrell Bank observatory EXCLUSIVE: 'No one, but no one thinks that this is a good idea' Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 13:14, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 13:1 The family of the late scien
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Family of Sir Bernard Lovell speak out to condemn funding cuts to Jodrell Bank observatory EXCLUSIVE: 'No one, but no one thinks that this is a good idea' Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 13:14, 31 Jul 2026 Updated 13:1 The family of the late scientist Sir Bernard Lovell have spoken out to condemn multi-million pound Government funding cuts to Jodrell Bank - the space observatory he created "No one, but no one thinks that this is a good idea," Sir Bernard's daughter, Judy Spence, told the Manchester Evening News today on behalf of generations of the family Ms Spence went on to challenge senior members of the Science and Technology Facilities Council - which has announced a vast cost-cutting drive - to visit Jodrell Bank and meet scientists and staff 'involved in the extraordinary work there'. "They will be inspired," she added The M.E.N. has launched a campaign to save deep space science at the observatory - and the working life of its iconic telescope, The Lovell Telescope A pioneering figure of British science, Sir Bernard was a founder of Jodrell Bank. Working with engineer Charles Husband, they conceived and designed what was then the world's biggest steerable radio telescope

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Flanked by police and surrounded by cameras, the moment fraudster Pamela Gwinnett was arrested Pamela Gwinnett, 63, fled to Tenerife in a bid to escape justice - but returned to Manchester Airport last night News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking Pamela Gwinnett, dubbed the 'Black Widow', fled the UK for Tenerife while awaiting trial for theft and fraud by abuse of position in 2025. In her absence, the 63-year-old was handed a six-year jail sentence A huge operation was launched by Greater Manchester Police and the National Crime Agency to bring Gwinnett back to the UK to face justice. Earlier this month she was detained by Spanish Police and last night (July 30), she landed at Manchester Airport where she was arrested GMP has today (July 31) released body-worn camera footage the moment she was arrested and put into the back of a police van outside Terminal 3. Gwinnett was flanked by two armed National Crime Agency officers as she was escorted out of the building Police then met her outside, with the footage showing the moment she was arrested. Gwinnett, who was wearing sunglasses, a leopard print jacket, capri pants and gold trainers, replied 'OK' as an officer outlined the details of her arrest The footage also showed several photographers surrounding her. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Rochdale shisha lounge closed after deadly gas put customers' lives in danger The venue was found to have exposed both customers and workers to excessive levels of carbon monoxide Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 10:28, 31 Jul 202 A Greater Manchester Shisha lounge has been closed after excessive levels of carbon monoxide were found. Phantom The Lounge on Maclure Road, Rochdale , were ordered to close by Rochdale Council's environmental health service The closure order was granted at Manchester Magistrates' court on July 24 following evidence submitted by environmental health officers, alongside support from Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service officers and Greater Manchester Police The order for the premises to close came following a routine inspection, which found that Phantom the Lounge had been illegally operating due to smoking taking place on site in a substantially closed area, Rochdale Council said The council's environmental officers identified this as a clear violation of the Smoke-Free regulations under the Health Act 2006 In addition to the illegal smoking, hazardous practices in the kitchen were found to have put customers and workers at risk due to "excessively high levels of CO" (carbon monoxide) on site

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires Incredible drone footage shows huge scale of Tintwistle Moor wildfire The fire service said 'steady progress' is being made on the moorland as the A628 Woodhead Pass reopens News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 08:48, 31 Jul 2026 I A wildfire at Tintwistle Moor, near Glossop, first started burning on June 24. A major incident was then declared in the area on July 12 as hotspots took hold of a huge area of the moorland Emergency crews have been on the scene for weeks tackling the fire in challenging conditions amid dry and warm weather. Yesterday (July 30) the Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service (DFRS) shared drone footage, taken by the Derby Mountain Rescue Team, which showed the scale of the m The service said previously that the fire, which sent huge plumes of smoke across Greater Manchester at its height, was estimated to have burned 606 hectares - equivalent to 900 football pitches. The footage showed hotspots burning in the peat on the moorland The fire service said in the update on Wednesday that 'steady progress continues to be made' as crews work across four main sectors. DFRS said: "The incident remains divided into four sectors at present, allowing resources to be deployed effectively and ensuring all affected area "While overall progress remains positive, on-ground teams have seen a slight increase in hotspots within the Featherbed Moss sector following a shift in wind direction. Crews are actively targeting these areas and are monitoring conditions closely

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Macclesfield Macclesfield teen 'should still be here' after NHS failings lead to preventable death Neil and Louise Arrowsmith say their son Isaac, 19, "should still be here" after a coroner concluded that NHS failings at Macclesfield District General The parents of a 19-year-old suffering from a rare blood disorder have said their son "should still be here" after an inquest determined that "mistakes" in his treatment contributed to his preventable death Neil and Louise Arrowsmith's son Isaac was diagnosed with Haemoglobin Rainier disease – a rare inherited blood condition that significantly raises the risk of blood clots – at just 18 years old On December 19, 2025, aged 19, Isaac began experiencing chest pain and breathlessness and started coughing up blood He was diagnosed with pneumonia at Macclesfield District General Hospital and sent home without any tests being carried out to rule out a pulmonary embolism As his condition continued to deteriorate, Isaac returned to A&E on December 31, but was placed under a respiratory virtual ward – a service designed to deliver hospital-level care at home within 48 hours – rather than being admitted as an inpatient

evidence_packet.lead: Oldham Oldham woman the first person in the world to receive groundbreaking cancer therapy at The Christie 'I often think, 'I'm still here', and that's helped me think.
evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Oldham woman the first person in the world to receive groundbreaking cancer therapy at The Christie 'I often think, 'I'm still here', and that's helped me think. 'why can't I still be here in 10 years?' News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 06:22, A woman from Greater Manchest
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Oldham woman the first person in the world to receive groundbreaking cancer therapy at The Christie 'I often think, 'I'm still here', and that's helped me think. 'why can't I still be here in 10 years?' News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 06:22, A woman from Greater Manchester with advanced ovarian cancer has become the first patient in the world to receive a pioneering new therapy. Tracy Tomlinson, 58, was given the drug at the Christie in Manchester as part of a clinical trial evaluating a new type of treatment for sev The therapy, known as ZI-MA4-1, will be tested on people with ovarian cancer, lung cancer, sarcomas and head and neck cancer in a trial led by the Christie, with a site also at the Royal Marsden in London. Many people in the study have few other options for survival Mrs Tomlinson, from Chadderton, Oldham, has already beaten the odds of staying alive, having undergone surgery and several rounds of chemotherapy since she was diagnosed in 2020 The new therapy works by combining two powerful methods in fighting cancer. Firstly, it harnesses the body’s natural killer (NK) cells, which are specialist immune cells that destroy abnormal ones Secondly, T-cell receptors (TCRs) on the cells are engineered to recognise and target tumours producing a protein called Mage-A4. Mage-A4 is found in several types of cancer and experts believe it is an ideal target for attacking abnormal cells

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics Mayors to get bigger share of income tax as part of Government's shake up of power Prime Minister Andy Burnham will give local leaders more flexibility to keep their revenue but it's not clear yet how much they will receive. Iram Ramzan repor News Iram Ramzan 22:30, 30 Jul 2026 Regional mayors will get a share of income tax revenue in what the Government says is the biggest transfer of power, funding and responsibility from Westminster in a generation The new system will give local leaders more freedom and flexibility to keep the revenue generated in their regions without being told by Whitehall how to spend it From April 2027, mayors will retain a greater share of business rates and from spring 2028 they will receive a share of income tax revenue. It is not yet clear what percentage of income tax the mayors will receive, but further details are expected during the autumn budget Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: “I said we'd take power out of Westminster and carry it into every postcode in the country. The 63-year-old was sentenced to six years in jail for several offences, including fraud by abuse of position and theft She tried to escape justice by absconding to Spain, however, the National Crime Agency and Spanish Police secured her extradition and arrest earlier this month As she made her way from Terminal 3 Arrivals lounge to the back of a police van, Gwinnett wore sunglasses, a leopard print jacket, capri pants and gold trainers. She was flanked by two armed National Crime Agency officers A smile as she exited quickly turned into a solemn look once she spotted cameras pointed at her. While being escorted to GMP officers, she remained silent as she was asked if she wanted to apologise to her victim's family, and if she was worried that her sentence will be extended

evidence_packet.lead: Stockport 'Sorry!': Stockport council boss speaks out as nearly 900 bins go uncollected In an update, councillor Jake Austin apologised after hundreds were 'blindsided' by a recent change News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:16, 30 Jul 2026 The Stockport council boss in
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport 'Sorry!': Stockport council boss speaks out as nearly 900 bins go uncollected In an update, councillor Jake Austin apologised after hundreds were 'blindsided' by a recent change News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:16, 30 Jul 2026 The Stockport council boss in
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport 'Sorry!': Stockport council boss speaks out as nearly 900 bins go uncollected In an update, councillor Jake Austin apologised after hundreds were 'blindsided' by a recent change News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:16, 30 Jul 2026 The Stockport council boss in charge of bin services has apologised after hundreds were ‘blindsided’ when their wheelies were not collected. Councillor Jake Austin said nearly 900 bins had not been collected and they were reviewing the situation so it does not happen again A July 2026 reminder sent to Totally Local Company (TLC), which operates Stockport’s bin services, instructed staff not to collect wheelie bins where the lid is open . While that is understood to not be a new policy, the new enforcement of this rule left hundreds of people with u People have been left angry as a result of this with opposition parties criticising the Liberal Democrat-run council over the situation . One councillor said: “It’s all a bit of a farce from my perspective.” The change has been brought in because of safety issues caused by bin lids being open. In 2016, a Stockport bin man was left fighting for his life with a broken sternum and ribs after a bin dropped from the back of a lorry It is understood an open bin increases the risk workers might incorrectly place the bin on the back of the lorry due to poor visibility. This increases the chance of similar incidents occurring again as well as litter to spill out onto the road

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A decade on, it's one of Altrincham's quiet success stories Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Ed Bright gave up a secure career at one of the world's biggest banks to teach himself to brew beer from scratch. Ten years on, Stubborn Mule Brewery & Tap has become one of Altrincham's most quietly cherished local businesses - and Ed still make When Ed Bright left his job at the BNY Mellon bank in 2015 with nothing but a personal loan, a borrowed shed in Timperley and a pile of brewing books, some may have questioned the wisdom of his decision A decade on, Stubborn Mule is one of Altrincham's quiet success stories - and Ed is still the only one making the beer Appropriately enough, it is a back story built on a stubborn refusal to give up. Ed spent 12 years in banking, working up to a decent middle management level, but by the time Lehman Brothers collapsed in 2008 he was watching colleagues disappear without replacement "It just wasn't doing it for me," he says. With his wife Swan expecting their second child, he made the call. "There was no point getting hung up about sitting behind a desk for the next 10 years. I wanted a challenge."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The application related to a site off Hasty Lane Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council has refused permission in principle for up to nine homes on land off Hasty Lane in Hale Barns The application, submitted on behalf of Matthew Welch by Chorley-based MWT Planning, sought to establish the principle of residential development on a parcel of grassland adjacent to 1 Hasty Lane. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Firefighters are still tackling the blaze at Dove Stone Reservoir in Saddleworth, which broke out on 11 July after a period of hot weather and low rainfall, before merging with other wildfires For those living in nearby Greenfield, road closures and the near-constant movement of fire engines have become a regular sight Deborah Hill, who works in interior design shop My Secret Boutique, said: "I think it's worrying about what is up there with the animals and wildlife and how long it will take for it to recover." She told the Local Democracy Reporting Service : "The fires are happening every year and they are getting worse every year. This is a bad one because it has gone on for weeks. That is worrying." While things have quietened now, she said: "Every day you generally see about six fire engines going past. You might see at least two police cars. Sirens all the time. It's like being in the city "It just makes you sad. You feel like you have been hurt. This is our land. It's just really sad."

This is the most effective way to reduce exposure to wildfire smoke Wildfire smoke can irritate the eyes, nose, throat and lungs. Most healthy people will only experience temporary symptoms, but smoke can have a greater impact on babies and young children, older people, pregnant people, and those with existing heart or lung conditions For most people any symptoms will be temporary and will quickly disappear once you are away from the smoke. T At the same time, Oldham's combined NEET and Not Known (NK) rate has fallen to 4.6%, down 1.1 percentage points from 2024/25. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

title: Young Musician's Summer School

evidence_packet.title: Young Musician's Summer School
evidence_packet.lead: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer!
evidence_packet.summary: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! […] The post Young Musician’s Summer School appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Young Musician’s Summer School . Young Musician’s Summer School. . Book here . . . . . . . Friday | 03.07.2026 . . . World of Music . Share . . . . --> . . We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club , or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! . . . . . Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. . . . . We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument.. . . Snacks and drinks provided, and pizzas on the final day. Please bring your own packed lunch to sessions Monday-Thursday.. . Dates: Monday 17th – Friday 21st August. Times: 10:00-16:30 Monday-Thursday, then a performance for friends and family on Friday at 13:00 (students will be expected to come in at 10:00 sharp on the Friday).. Ages: 12-18 years old. Cost: £150 for the full course. Bursaries are available for those on lower income – please email learning@bandonthewall.org to arrange this.. . Spaces are limited – Book here . . . Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

In this show Mike talks about doing psychedelics with his brother, an entanglement with a Spanish Sausage Dog named Nino, and many other such rotten adventures ‘ Ireland has yet another legendary comedian ‘ – Dan Nightingale Irish farmer’s son, and general Nasty Character Mike Rice is one of Ireland and the UK’s fastest rising comedy stars. Having started comedy in 2016 Mike has amassed a large online following from podcast and stand-up clips, regularly getting millions of views on various platforms Mike began stand-up comedy in Chicago, where within two years he was working regularly at the most prestigious clubs in the city, including The Laugh Factory. He has since returned home because his mother made him, and has been quickly rising in the Irish and European scene, play Mike brought his first solo show The Best Boy in Ireland to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival 2018, in what was a sold-out run, and performed that same show to sold-out rooms at the Perth Fringe Festival in 2019 As well as co-hosting Mike & Vittorio’s Guide to Parenting with Vittorio Angelone, and Big Mike and The Chief with Rob Moriarty, Mike has appeared multiple times on smash hit podcast Have a Word and released his first comedy special in October 2023

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The original team behind Ramona and The Firehouse will open the two-floor restaurant, bar and music venue this September Go to Manchester's Finest X profile A new Latin American-inspired barbecue restaurant, bar and late-night venue is set to open in Manchester’s Northern Quarter this September Dahlia is the latest project from WANT Studios, the creative hospitality studio run by Andy Marshall, Andy Windsor, Liam McCue and Adelaide Winter The WANT Studios team were the original creatives behind Manchester venues including Ramona and The Firehouse.
