Eats Legendary landlady of The Peveril of the Peak pub has passed away Nancy had been at the helm of the boozer for 55 years Daisy Jackson - 30th July 2026 Nancy Swanick, the legendary landlady behind Manchester’s much-loved Peveril of the Peak pub, has died. The pub shared a statement today to confirm that Nancy, 96, who was the pub’s landlady for more than 55 years, passed away earlier this week. --> She’s become something of an icon across the UK and was the oldest and longest-serving landlady in the country. The Peveril of the Peak – or simply The Pev, to most of us – had just been named the best pub in the UK earlier this week. The Pev has now assured fans that the pub will remain in the Swanick family, even without Nancy at its helm. ADVERTISEMENT They said in their touching statement: “We will continue to cherish it as we did Nancy.” In their full statement, The Peveril of the Peak wrote: “We are sad to say that our beloved Nancy, landlady for over 55 years, passed away peacefully on 28th July. ADVERTISEMENT View this post on Instagram A post shared by The Pev (@thepeverilofthepeak) “Nancy always kept up to date with news about the Pev and we told her about our new accolade of Best Pub in the UK a few days ago. “The Pev will stay in the Swanick family and we will continue to cherish it as we did Nancy. “The pub will remain open thanks to our brilliant staff and, if you pop in anytime soon, please raise your glass to the wonder that was Nancy. ADVERTISEMENT “With love, The Swanicks.” RIP to a true local legend. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Our Mayor is now our Prime Minister, and the skills agenda he's brought to Downing Street is one we've lived and breathed for over a decade Andy Burnham has spent some of his first fortnight in office setting out plans to reshape technical education and get more young people into work, built on the MBacc model developed here in Greater Manchester. This is familiar ground for us. For over ten years Manchester Digital That gap has become harder to bridge, economic uncertainty, higher costs and cautious hiring are playing their part as is AI, which is starting to strip out the routine tasks junior roles were built on. This has resulted in the entry-level jobs young people used to start in being Alan Milburn's interim review, published in May, put a shortage of entry-level jobs at the centre of a "generational fault line", with one in eight young people now not in education, employment or training. His recommendations come in the autumn, but the direction is already clea We sit right in the middle of this, we represent the employers in this sector so we hear it from both sides, everyone knows that the talent pipeline is crucial to whether the sector thrives but it's harder to do in practice than it sounds. It's almost never a question of goodwill There's a commercial reason to act too, public sector procurement is almost certain to start weighting placements and apprenticeships as part of its social value requirements, which means companies bidding for public contracts will increasingly need to show what they already offe

The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

Being in an environment that’s detached from the outside world where you can fully devote your attention to a single task is something w In Manchester we’re spoilt for choice of places to cultivate these skills. Bee Creative Studio hosts life drawing workshops for people of all abilities at various venues in the Northern Quarter . The sessions run sporadically so be sure to check the website for upcoming dates. Th Life drawing isn’t about just drawing nude figures, it is a way of challenging your own perceptions of beauty. In the setting of a class you are part of a larger group, this is a brilliant way to share the knowledge of those around and let yourself be inspired by their ideas. Lif The sessions are untutored but a range of media is provided such as pencils, pastels, sharpeners, rubbers and paper. Artists are also encouraged to bring their own materials should they wish to work with something different

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City reporter in Hong Kong Published 29 July 2026 Manchester City returned to pre-season training last week and midfielder Jack Grealish was spotted among the players who had reported for duty But any immediate hopes of seeing the 30-year-old donning a City shirt once more were dashed on Tuesday night when he missed out on a seat on the plane for the club's tour of Hong Kong and Seoul over the next 11 days Responding to a social media post that said he had been left out of City's pre-season tour, Grealish wrote: "Just to let you know I'm still recovering from an injury so I'm not training yet "Haven't been 'left out' so stop talking poo poo thanks." Grealish sustained a season-ending foot injury in January during a loan spell at Everton , where he was starting to recapture his best form, and it is too early to speculate what the future might hold The injury ended not only his time at Hill Dickinson Stadium but an outside shot at playing at the World Cup for England too

evidence_packet.evidence_text: 8 ноября 2026 года в Indigo at The O2 состоится концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне Имя Горана Бреговича давно стало символом целого музыкального мира. Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Именно эта атмосфера сформировала композитора, впоследствии воз Впоследствии музыка Бреговича вышла за рамки концертных площадок. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. evidence_packet.lead: A monthly meetup in Manchester for the people doing account-based marketing.
evidence_packet.summary: A monthly meetup in Manchester for the people doing account-based marketing. A place to meet others in the same line of work, share what you know, and pick up ideas from everyone else in the room
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A monthly meetup in Manchester for the people doing account-based marketing. A place to meet others in the same line of work, share what you know, and pick up ideas from everyone else in the room. Come and join us, whether you're just getting started with account-based marketing Most marketing advice assumes your market is enormous. Email campaigns to ten thousand people. Ads that only pay off at volume. Growth playbooks written for products that could have a million users. All of it built for mass scale Plenty of B2B SaaS companies don't work that way, especially the ones selling a mix of software and done-for-you service. If every company that could ever buy from you fits on one list - 500, 1000, maybe 5000 names - the mass-scale playbook doesn't just underperform. It burns thr Regular marketing is a numbers game: reach as many people as possible and let a small percentage become customers. Account-based marketing starts from the other end. You write down the specific companies you want to win - your shortlist - then get to know each one properly and ma The catch: the people doing this work are usually figuring it out alone, inside their own companies. There's no shortage of rooms for mass-market growth talk. There hasn't been one for this. That's why The Shortlist exists - once a month, the people doing account-based marketing CMOs, Marketing managers and marketing specialists at B2B SaaS companies whose growth depends on winning a specific, nameable set of accounts rather than reaching as many people as possible

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Economic Development Politics Andy Burnham says 'best day of my life' as No 10 North opens in Manchester Prime Minister Andy Burnham has opened the doors to No 10 North in Manchester Comments Economic Development Kirstie McCrum Deputy Head of News, Live News Network 14:49, 24 Jul No 10 North has welcomed visitors for the Prime Minister's inaugural meeting to be conducted at his Manchester headquarters. Andy Burnham described it as the 'best day of my life' while addressing personnel at Heron House, close to Manchester's Albert Square, on Friday morning Addressing staff upon his arrival, Mr Burnham said: "I cannot tell you what a proud moment this is. I think this might be the best day of my life "I'm not joking. I know you think I am, but I'm not. Things are just completely coming full circle here, for me to be here with you all in the heart of Manchester this Friday morning at the end of a fairly big week is just everything to me." He continued: "Things are just completely coming full circle here for me, and to be here with you all in the heart of Manchester this Friday morning, at the end of a fairly big week, is just everything to me because it's almost exactly 35 years since I left this city as a recentl "That really is an experience that I've never forgotten, my generation of people growing up here. And it's true of places all over the country to get on in life, you had to leave where you where you were because things weren't here."
